evidence.reference_title: An in vitro human vessel model to study Neisseria meningitidis colonization and vascular damages.
evidence.snippet: To overcome these limitations, we developed a laser photoablation-generated, three-dimensional microfluidic model of meningococcal vascular colonization, a human-specific bacterium that causes sepsis and meningitis.

nodes.description: Meningococcal adhesion to endothelial cells activates ADAM10 and sheds the endothelial protein C receptor from the endothelial surface, reducing local generation of activated protein C.

evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate that meningococcal adhesion on endothelial cells impairs the activation of PC by inducing an ADAM10-mediated shedding of EPCR.

evidence.reference_title: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome, septic adrenal apoplexy.
evidence.snippet: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome is a rare but potentially fatal disorder of the adrenal gland characterized by bilateral adrenal hemorrhage. It is classically a result of meningococcal sepsis and presents acutely with features of shock, petechial rashes, abdominal pain, and non-specific symptoms such as headache, fatigue, and vomiting.

evidence.reference_title: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) in meningococcal septic shock and experimental human endotoxemia.
evidence.snippet: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor concentration in blood was increased during meningococcal disease and highest in the patients presenting with shock compared with patients without shock.

readouts.interpretation: Higher MIF tracks with shock and multiple inflammatory cytokines in invasive meningococcal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Does granulocyte colony-stimulating factor ameliorate the proinflammatory response in human meningococcal septic shock?
evidence.snippet: The median levels of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor in shock and nonshock patients were 1.7 x 10(6) and 8.1 x 10(2) pg/mL; interleukin-10, 2.1 x 10(4) and 4 x 10(1) pg/mL; number of N. meningitidis DNA copies, 2.9 x 10(7) and <10(3)/mL; and lipopolysaccharide, 105 and <0.04 endotoxin units/mL, respectively.

readouts.interpretation: Higher N. meningitidis DNA copy number reports a larger bloodstream bacterial burden that tracks with persistent shock.

nodes.description: Acute meningococcal plasma and peripheral blood mononuclear cells exposed to meningococci contain 10-25 kDa proteinaceous myocardial-depressant activity, adding a reversible cardiac-depression arm to septic shock.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a myocardial depressant factor in meningococcal septicemia.
evidence.snippet: Serum from patients with meningococcal disease had myocardial depressant activity. This activity was also present in whole blood and peripheral blood mononuclear cells exposed to meningococci. Myocardial depressant activity was found to be heat stable, proteinaceous, and of a molecular weight range of 10-25 kDa.

evidence.reference_title: Meningococcal purpura fulminans and severe myocarditis with clinical meningitis but no meningeal inflammation: a case report.
evidence.snippet: On day 2, after initial improvement, a recurrence of hypotension led to the diagnosis of acute meningococcal myocarditis, which evolved favourably within a week.

nodes.description: Encapsulated meningococci survive in blood when bacterial complement evasion and a host with insufficient serum bactericidal activity permit escape from membrane-attack-complex killing, causing high-grade meningococcal bacteremia.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Spectrum of a Large Cohort With Total and Sub-total Complement Deficiencies.
evidence.snippet: Our study confirms the strong association of meningococcal infections with terminal pathway deficiency and highlights the risk of pneumococcal and auto-immune diseases in the classical and alternative pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Deficient alternative complement pathway activation due to factor D deficiency by 2 novel mutations in the complement factor D gene in a family with meningococcal infections.
evidence.snippet: This deficiency abolishes alternative-pathway dependent complement activation by N meningitidis, and leads to an increased susceptibility to invasive meningococcal disease.

nodes.description: Suspected meningococcemia is treated immediately with bactericidal parenteral antibiotics, with third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone or cefotaxime widely used in secondary care.

evidence.reference_title: Antibiotic resistance among invasive Neisseria meningitidis isolates in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (2010/11 to 2018/19).
evidence.snippet: In the UK, penicillin is administered to patients in primary care whilst third generation cephalosporins, cefotaxime and ceftriaxone, are administered in secondary care.

nodes.description: Shared bedrooms, more people per bedroom, and frequent pub/party attendance mark crowded close-contact settings that increase meningococcal carriage.

evidence.reference_title: Meningococcal Carriage among Adolescents after Mass Meningococcal C Conjugate Vaccination Campaigns in Salvador, Brazil.
evidence.snippet: Factors associated with carriage were having only one, shared, bedroom in the household (PR, 2.02; 95% CI, 0.99-4.12, p = 0.05); the mother being the only smoker in the home (PR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.16-5.29; p = 0.01); and going to pubs/parties more than 5 times/month (PR, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.38-4.92; p = 0.02).

evidence.reference_title: Carriage of N. lactamica in a population at high risk of meningococcal disease.
evidence.snippet: Factors associated with a significant (P < 0.05) increase in the likelihood of carriage included runny nose, the number of people per bedroom and youth.

nodes.description: High meningococcal and lipooligosaccharide burdens stimulate monocytes and other innate immune cells, producing a systemic cytokine response in which LPS and IL-10 concentrations track severe systemic meningococcal disease.

evidence.reference_title: IL-10 immunodepletion from meningococcal sepsis plasma induces extensive changes in gene expression and cytokine release in stimulated human monocytes.
evidence.snippet: The severity of systemic meningococcal disease (SMD) correlates to plasma concentrations of LPS and IL-10, with the highest levels detected in non-survivors.

nodes.description: Capsular conjugate vaccines against serogroups A, C, W, and Y and protein-based serogroup B vaccines induce bactericidal antibodies that prevent invasive meningococcal disease before bloodstream invasion.

evidence.reference_title: Severe meningococcal infection: a review of epidemiology, diagnosis, and management.
evidence.snippet: Vaccines have reduced the incidence of infection with certain non-B meningococcal serogroups, and new serotype B vaccines are on the horizon.

evidence.reference_title: Vaccination of Infants with Meningococcal Group B Vaccine (4CMenB) in England.
evidence.snippet: From September 2015 through August 2018, the incidence of meningococcal group B disease in England (average annual birth cohort, approximately 650,000 infants) was significantly lower in vaccine-eligible cohorts than the expected incidence (63 observed cases as compared with 253 expected cases; incidence rate ratio, 0.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.19 to 0.36), with a 75% reduction in age groups that were fully eligible for vaccination.

nodes.description: Patients receiving terminal-complement inhibitors need MenACWY and MenB vaccination with antibiotic prophylaxis around treatment initiation because pharmacologic C5 blockade leaves residual breakthrough meningococcal risk.

evidence.reference_title: Beyond Vaccination: Persistent Meningococcal Risk in Anti-C5-Treated aHUS-Case Report and Review of Literature.

evidence.reference_title: Severe meningococcal infection: a review of epidemiology, diagnosis, and management.

evidence.reference_title: Meningococcal prophylaxis in neurological diseases treated with complement inhibitors: an expert consensus for Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
